subject: Civil Engineering
title: Environmental Impacts of Dams
description: A 60-second lesson on Environmental Impacts of Dams.

hook.text: Dams provide power and water — but they devastate river ecosystems and displace communities.

buildup.text: Dams block fish migration — salmon can't reach spawning grounds. Populations collapse.

discovery.text: Reservoirs flood valleys — destroying habitats, farmland, and sometimes entire towns.

twist.text: Downstream rivers lose sediment, nutrients, and natural flood pulses — deltas erode and shrink.

climax.text: Dam removal is growing — the US removed over 2,000 dams to restore rivers.

punchline.text: Every dam is a trade-off — power and water versus ecosystems and communities.

quiz.question: Why does dam removal restore river ecosystems?
options: It allows fish to migrate freely and restores natural sediment and flood cycles
Removing concrete adds nutrients to the river water
It increases water temperature to levels preferred by native fish species
